newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks sprint home to higher close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks sprint home to higher close.

text.p: SPI futures 2250 +14 US 30yr cl 7.08 -0.03
S&P500(Globex) n/a NZSE40 2213.90 +1.67
*Stocks fly home to close near highs. Resurgent BHP and buoyant CRA lead the way. Turnover 305.93 million shares, value A$690.76 million, 984 stocks traded, 283 steady, 402 up, 299 down
The Australian share market flew home in the last hour of trading on Friday to close barely a whisker off the day's highs.
A resurgent BHP, as short sellers covered positions, led the late charge with a buoyant CRA in solid support after being severely oversold on Thursday.
At 4.30 p.m. (0630 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 15.7 points up at 2,252.3. September share price index futures were 14 points higher at 2,250, a 2.3 point discount to the underlying index.
Citing short selling and active trading in BHP warrants, brokers said the late rush of blood had startled the bourse out of its Friday afternoon, pre-weekend stupor.
"It really kicked up at the end with a lot of short covering in BHP shares and solid trade in the warrants," said dealer Peter Struk of Reynolds and Co.
Other players echoed similar sentiments, saying Thursday's selldown in the miners had been overdone.
"There was plenty of plays between warrants and the (BHP) shares but really it was a case of Thursday being overdone," said a Sydney-based dealer.
"CRA has been on a winner all day after Thursday. Their result came in around what we expected and they are looking better further down the track," he said.

Outside the major miners, perennial takeover target, gaming machine manufacturer AWA Ltd, broke through two year highs as traders mulled the possibility of a bid as the company continued to realise non-core assets.
With the results season reaching its climax today, the major result came from conglomerate Pacific Dunlop whose full year loss of A$132.74 million was within expectations and caused few flutters.
Troubled pay TV operator Australis Media continued to bleed red ink, posting a full year net loss of A$220.98 million.

On the plus side, though, the company said it had secured extra equity commitments to its recapitalisation plan and had received written indications from its U.S. bondholders to allow the plan to proceed.
Other results came from retailer Harvey Norman which turned in a slightly lower full year net profit of A$30.41 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about four to three, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian bonds were largely taken up by the rollover to December futures contracts ahead of Monday's September expiries and as the market awaited the second stage of key U.S. inflation data later on Friday, traders said.
By 4.35 p.m. (0635 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 8.10 percent, unchanged from Thursday's close.

The Australian dollar spent an uneventful day trading a narrow range after overnight selling had seen it fall through support, with talk of a options strangle limiting the currency's movement. By 5.25 p.m. (0725 GMT), the local dollar was quoted at US$0.7961/66.
